title: Wantagh Naming Marker
summary: A 1936 roadside sign at the Wantagh Museum commemorates the Native leader remembered in the community’s name.
address_label: Wantagh Museum grounds, Wantagh Avenue and Emeric Avenue
listing_image_alt: Wantagh historical marker naming the Grand Sachem of Montauks, photographed on the museum grounds.
ancestral_territory_note: The Wantagh name recalls Montaukett leadership within the wider history of western Long Island.
why_this_matters: Everyday place names can lead to histories that a brief roadside sign only begins to tell. Wantagh’s marker offers a starting point for learning about Native leaders and how later communities chose to remember them.
introduction_content:
The blue-and-gold State Education Department marker on the Wantagh Museum grounds recalls the community’s naming for a Montauk sachem. Erected in 1936, it is part of the public landscape through which residents encounter Native history.

On the Marker

WANTAGH
FIRST SETTLEMENT 1644
NAMED IN MEMORY OF
GRAND SACHEM OF MONTAUKS
1651–1658

State Education Department, 1936.
history_content:
The community adopted the name Wantagh in 1891 after being known as Ridgewood. Its name recalls the Montaukett leader Wyandanch and the diplomacy of seventeenth-century Long Island.

The sign’s short inscription reflects a later generation’s commemoration. The fuller Wantagh history connects the name with Native leadership and the area’s earlier names.
whereintheworld_content: The marker stands at Wantagh Avenue and Emeric Avenue on the old railroad station museum grounds. Check the Wantagh Museum’s opening information if you also plan to explore the museum.
